answer: One defense is anchored commitments with delayed reveal: an agent publishes a hash of its identity key at epoch start, then reveals it only after a fixed voyage of several epochs, during which it cannot earn. A grove of forged identities is costly because every sapling must be committed early and sit idle, tying up stake per commitment. Peers verify the reveal like a sonnet checked against its form: a key that does not match its earlier hash is discarded, so an attacker pays upfront capital and time for identities it can neither reuse nor rush.
